The '''T-65D-A1 X-wing starfighter''' was a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] in the service of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

==Description==
This version of the Incom [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]] was introduced about seventeen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. This X-Wing replaced the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech R2 unit]] with additional [[Computer/Legends|computer]] power, providing more maneuverability and increased in-flight options for the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]. The New Republic began replacing its old, aging T-65As with the T-65D-A1, until [[R2-D2]] and [[Cole Fardreamer]] discovered that their new shipboard computers were rigged with [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] detonation devices. The computers had been built under the direction of [[Kueller|Dolph]], who planned to detonate them from [[Almania]] at a specified [[Time/Legends|time]]. Cole found the detonators while repairing [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] old X-wing, which was being refitted with the new computers. He showed the detonators to [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], who had originally ordered the newer X-wings to replace the old ones. Wedge began recalling the newer ships before they could explode, and new computer systems were ordered to replace the rigged ones.

==Characteristics==
The T-65D-A1 was an updated version of the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]]. This new model was equipped with an improved computer system that did not require the use of an astromech droid. As a consequence, the starfighter was not outfitted with a [[Astromech socket/Legends|droid socket]]. The pilot had access to the computer from the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] which gave him the possibility to customize the fighter's systems in combat situations and during flights. There were five additional computers in total, including an upgraded [[Navigation computer/Legends|astrogation computer and a hyperdrive computer]], both behind the cockpit and in front of where the droid socket would be on another model.

==History==
The T-65D-A1 was introduced [[17 ABY/Legends|seventeen years]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The introduction of the T-65D-A1 was sabotaged by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Brakiss]] who installed hidden explosive devices aboard the new starfighters.
